slides.heading: append()
slides.body: append() is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: append()
slides.body: append() adds one new item to the end of a list. It is useful when new data arrives after the list already exists.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: append() is like adding a new item to the end of a grocery list.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.
